findings.title: MetricAlertDetectorHandler is now an uninstantiable abstract class
findings.body: MetricAlertDetectorHandler was changed from a concrete DetectorHandler whose evaluate() returned [] to a bare subclass of StatefulDetectorHandler. That base class declares abstract counter_names, get_dedupe_value, get_group_key_values, and build_occurrence_and_event_data, none of which this class implements. It is still assigned as MetricAlertFire.detector_handler, and Detector.detector_handler instantiates that class. Any detector with type metric_alert_fire will raise TypeError ('Can't instantiate abstract class') inside process_detectors instead of being skipped or returning no results.

findings.title: Occurrence hook cannot see the data packet that triggered it
findings.body: build_occurrence_and_event_data is only given group_key, an int value, and a PriorityLevel. evaluate() has the full DataPacket but never threads it (or the prior DetectorStateData) into the hook. Metric-alert style packets (QuerySubscriptionUpdate) carry the query id, timestamps, and evidence needed to build a real IssueOccurrence; a subclass cannot reach that payload except by stashing it as a side effect of get_dedupe_value/get_group_key_values. The first real implementation of this hook will either emit incomplete occurrences or rely on hidden instance state.

findings.title: Occurrence tests ignore the evaluated value, so wrong values still pass
findings.body: build_mock_occurrence_and_event accepts value but never uses it, and several assertions pass a value that does not match the packet (test_state_results_multi_group builds the group_2 expectation with 6 while group_vals has 10; test_results_on_change and test_dedupe expect value 6 for packets of 100 and 8). Because the helper ignores value, those tests still pass even if evaluate_group_key_value forwarded the wrong measurement into build_occurrence_and_event_data.
